title: The tipping taboo
paragraphs: It’s nice to go out for a meal at a restaurant. But what makes it extra special – apart from the food - is to receive attentive service from the staff. What can leave a bad taste in your mouth, though, is to be handed the bill and see that a service charge has been added. You’re faced with the dilemma of deciding to pay it, and whether you should add a tip on top.

Putting your hand in your pocket to reward good service is a personal choice, but it also depends on where you are in the world. What is the norm in one city is not necessarily the norm in another. In some places a tip is expected; but in others, good service should be expected and ought to be included in the price.

Adding an optional service charge to your bill certainly makes paying a tip less awkward because there’s no need to calculate the amount. But even though it’s not compulsory, you sometimes feel obliged to pay it. In the UK, where people tend to be too polite to complain, they might pay the service charge despite quietly complaining that the service they received was not up to scratch!

Choosing your own amount to tip may seem fairer, but should you pay it in cash or add it on to a credit card payment? And who will be the recipient? If we are to pay extra, we want to know it goes to the person who deserves it and that it’s not used as an alternative to paying someone a proper wage. In the UK in 2009, the law was changed after an outcry over staff being paid under the minimum wage and then topping up their wages with money they had earned in tips.

However, in the US it’s still customary to leave a gratuity because tips often make up a substantial part of a server’s income. Restaurant owner William Beckett told the BBC that in New York, for example, “There’s a tacit pressure to tip. But theoretically you (could) just stand up and walk out. You don’t. Everybody tips 20%.”

Maybe we should follow Japan’s approach, where tipping under any circumstance may seem rude because good service is standard and expected. Elsewhere, there are calls for restaurants to replace the tipping system with a so-called 'hospitality-included' charge – a single payment which covers both the meal and the service. This basically means, don’t tip - the price you see on the menu reflects the full cost of dining. That might make receiving the final bill easier to swallow!

vocabulary.entry: attentive service /əˈtentɪv ˈsɜːvɪs/ 周到的服务
vocabulary.example: The hotel is famous for its attentive service to every guest.
vocabulary.translation: 这家酒店以对每位客人的周到服务而闻名。

vocabulary.term: leave a bad taste in your mouth
vocabulary.entry: leave a bad taste in your mouth /liːv ə bæd teɪst ɪn jɔː maʊθ/ 让人心里不舒服；留下坏印象
vocabulary.example: The rude waiter left a bad taste in my mouth.
vocabulary.translation: 那个态度恶劣的服务员让我心里很不舒服。

vocabulary.entry: service charge /ˈsɜːvɪs tʃɑːdʒ/ 服务费
vocabulary.example: A 10% service charge is added to the bill in this restaurant.
vocabulary.translation: 这家餐厅的账单会加收10%的服务费。

vocabulary.entry: be faced with the dilemma /bi ˈfeɪst wɪð ðə dɪˈlemə/ 陷入两难境地
vocabulary.example: She was faced with the dilemma of choosing between work and family.
vocabulary.translation: 她陷入了在工作和家庭之间做选择的两难境地。

vocabulary.entry: norm /nɔːm/ n. 惯例；常态
vocabulary.example: It is a social norm to shake hands when meeting someone for the first time.
vocabulary.translation: 初次见面握手是一种社交惯例。

vocabulary.entry: awkward /ˈɔːkwəd/ adj. 尴尬的
vocabulary.example: I felt awkward when I realized I had mispronounced her name.
vocabulary.translation: 当我意识到自己念错了她的名字时，我感到很尴尬。

vocabulary.entry: compulsory /kəmˈpʌlsəri/ adj. 强制的；义务的
vocabulary.example: Wearing a seat belt is compulsory for all passengers.
vocabulary.translation: 所有乘客都必须系安全带。

vocabulary.entry: feel obliged to /fiːl əˈblaɪdʒd tu/ 觉得必须做；不得不做
vocabulary.example: I felt obliged to invite him to the party because he helped me a lot.
vocabulary.translation: 因为他帮了我很多，我觉得必须邀请他参加派对。

vocabulary.entry: not up to scratch /nɒt ʌp tu skrætʃ/ 未达标准；不尽如人意
vocabulary.example: The quality of the product is not up to scratch, so we need to improve it.
vocabulary.translation: 这款产品的质量未达标准，我们需要进行改进。

vocabulary.entry: recipient /rɪˈsɪpiənt/ n. 接受者；收件人
vocabulary.example: She was the recipient of the annual scholarship.
vocabulary.translation: 她是本年度奖学金的获得者。

vocabulary.entry: alternative /ɔːlˈtɜːnətɪv/ n. 替代品；选择
vocabulary.example: There is no effective alternative to this medicine for treating the disease.
vocabulary.translation: 治疗这种疾病，没有比这种药更有效的替代品了。

vocabulary.entry: outcry /ˈaʊtkraɪ/ n. 抗议；呐喊
vocabulary.example: The decision caused a public outcry among local residents.
vocabulary.translation: 这项决定引起了当地居民的公开抗议。

vocabulary.entry: top up /tɒp ʌp/ 补足；充值
vocabulary.example: I need to top up my phone with some credit before I go out.
vocabulary.translation: 出门前我得给手机充点话费。

vocabulary.entry: customary /ˈkʌstəməri/ adj. 习惯的；惯例的
vocabulary.example: It is customary to give gifts at Christmas in Western countries.
vocabulary.translation: 在西方国家，圣诞节送礼是一种习俗。

vocabulary.entry: gratuity /ɡrəˈtjuːəti/ n. 小费；赏钱
vocabulary.example: The gratuity is usually calculated as a percentage of the total bill.
vocabulary.translation: 小费的金额通常按账单总额的一定比例计算。

vocabulary.entry: substantial /səbˈstænʃl/ adj. 大量的；相当可观的
vocabulary.example: The project has brought substantial benefits to the local community.
vocabulary.translation: 这个项目为当地社区带来了可观的效益。

vocabulary.entry: tacit /ˈtæsɪt/ adj. 心照不宣的；默示的
vocabulary.example: There is a tacit agreement between them to keep the secret.
vocabulary.translation: 他们之间有一个保守秘密的默契。

vocabulary.entry: circumstance /ˈsɜːkəmstəns/ n. 情况；情形
vocabulary.example: Under no circumstances should you leave the child alone at home.
vocabulary.translation: 无论在何种情况下，你都不应该把孩子单独留在家里。

vocabulary.entry: call for /kɔːl fɔː/ 呼吁；要求
vocabulary.example: Environmental groups are calling for stricter laws to protect wildlife.
vocabulary.translation: 环保组织呼吁出台更严格的法律来保护野生动物。

vocabulary.entry: hospitality-included charge /ˌhɒspɪˈtæləti ɪnˈkluːdɪd tʃɑːdʒ/ 服务费全包收费
vocabulary.example: The restaurant uses a hospitality-included charge to avoid disputes over tipping.
vocabulary.translation: 这家餐厅采用服务费全包的收费方式，避免因小费产生纠纷。

vocabulary.entry: reflect /rɪˈflekt/ v. 反映；体现
vocabulary.example: The results of the survey reflect people's attitudes towards the new policy.
vocabulary.translation: 调查结果反映了人们对新政策的态度。

vocabulary.entry: easier to swallow /ˈiːziə tu ˈswɒləʊ/ 更容易接受；心里更好受
vocabulary.example: The news of the pay rise made the long working hours easier to swallow.
vocabulary.translation: 加薪的消息让长时间工作这件事变得更容易让人接受了。
